chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Yaqub ibn Yazeed from Muhammad ibn Marazim and Yazeed ibn Hammad all from Abdillah ibn Sinan, in what I think, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: If someone who is not a friend of Ali (peace be upon him) came to the Euphrates, and its water was clear on both sides of him, gushing forth, and he reached out with his hand and said 'Bismillah', and when he finished he said 'Alhamdulillah', it would be like (drinking) gushing blood or flesh of a pig.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the purity of water drunk by non-walis of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the concept of *al-walayah* (spiritual guardianship) as a determinant of ontological purity, suggesting that the spiritual status of the drinker transforms the nature of the consumed water. While standard recitations like *Bismillah* are present, the absence of the specific 'friendship' with Imam Ali renders the water spiritually impure, likened to blood or pork. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the intrinsic connection between the believer's spiritual rank and the purity of their physical and metaphysical reality.

en.hubeali: H 14611 – Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Marazim and Yazeed Bin Hammaad altogether from Abu Abdullah Bin Sinan in what I think he narrated, who has narrated the following:

Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘If someone who is not a friend of Aliasws came to Al-Furaat and there was clear water on both his sides whilst he lowers his palms to take it by his hands, and says, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj’, and when he is free from that he says, ‘Praise be to Allahazwj’, it would be like (drinking) gushing blood or flesh of the swine’. (In another Hadith if a Momin drinks water like this it would keep on praising Allah in his stomach as long as it stays there).
en.sarwar: 163. Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Marazim and Yazeed Bin Hammaad altogether from Abu Abdullah Bin Sinan in what I think he narrated, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said: ‘

If someone who is not a friend of Ali (a.s.) came to Al-Furaat and there was clear water on both his sides whilst he lowers his palms to take it by his hands, and says, ‘In the Name of Allah (azwj)’, and when he is free from that he says, ‘Praise be to Allah (azwj)’, it would be like (drinking) gushing blood or flesh of the swine’. (In another Hadith if a Momin drinks water like this it would keep on praising Allah in his stomach as long as it stays there).
